items.markdown:
Androgenetic alopecia is `a common, hereditary form of progressive hair loss driven by genetics and the hormone dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which shrinks hair follicles over time`.[[1]](https://ishrs.org/androgenetic-alopecia/)[[2]](https://southlakedermatology.com/services/androgenic-alopecia/)[[3]](https://www.americanhairloss.org/types-of-hair-loss/androgeneticalopecia/)

### Symptoms and Patterns

- **Men (Male Pattern Baldness):** Hair loss starts above the temples and at the crown, forming a receding "M" shape or progressive vertex balding.[[1]](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/androgenetic-alopecia/)[[2]](https://southlakedermatology.com/services/androgenic-alopecia/)
- **Women (Female Pattern Hair Loss):** Hair thins broadly across the upper scalp and the central part line widens, though the front hairline usually stays intact and total baldness is rare.[[1]](https://southlakedermatology.com/services/androgenic-alopecia/)[[2]](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/androgenetic-alopecia/)
- **Scalp Changes:** Thick terminal hairs gradually shrink into short, thin, non-pigmented vellus hairs over successive growth cycles.[[1]](https://www.americanhairloss.org/types-of-hair-loss/androgeneticalopecia/)[[2]](https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/1070167-overview)

### Classification Scales

- **Norwood Scale:** Measures male-pattern progression across stages 1 through 7.
- **Ludwig Scale:** Measures female-pattern hair thinning across stages 1 through 3.[[1]](https://ishrs.org/androgenetic-alopecia/)

### Common Treatments

- **FDA-Approved Medications:** Topical or oral minoxidil to stimulate growth, and oral finasteride to block DHT conversion.
- **Off-Label & Alternative Options:** Oral dutasteride, spironolactone (for women), topical clascoterone, and low-level light therapy.
- **Procedural Options:** Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) therapy, microneedling, and surgical hair transplantation (FUE or FUT).[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9298335/)[[2]](https://ishrs.org/androgenetic-alopecia/)[[3]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10173235/)

For detailed clinical guidance and treatment pathways, you can explore updates via the [International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery](https://ishrs.org/androgenetic-alopecia/) or medical references on [MedlinePlus Genetics](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/androgenetic-alopecia/).[[1]](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/androgenetic-alopecia/)[[2]](https://ishrs.org/androgenetic-alopecia/)Would you like to focus on **treatments for men or women** , or do you want more information on **side effects and costs** of specific medications?
